docs.title: MSF Laravel Inventory
docs.text: msflib/inventory is the inventory domain package for the MSF Laravel ecosystem. It provides reusable stock and inventory primitives that can be integrated into Laravel apps with shared GraphQL and common-package conventions.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
This package provides:

  • inventory domain models and Laravel integration
  • GraphQL access surfaces for inventory data
  • integration with shared MSF packages such as msflib/common and msflib/graphql
  • reusable domain conventions for business-facing inventory flows

docs.title: Operational notes
docs.text:
• keep this package focused on inventory concerns
  • prefer shared package integration over app-specific code
  • keep API and schema conventions consistent with the broader MSF stack

docs.title: Package overview
docs.text: The msflib/inventory package is part of the MSF Laravel ecosystem and provides the reusable inventory domain layer for Laravel applications and packages. It focuses on core inventory models and package integration rather than generic application behavior.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
This package is intended to cover:

  • package-level configuration and bootstrapping
  • inventory domain model registration
  • GraphQL or schema-based inventory access
  • coordination with common/shared package services

docs.title: Expected integration pattern
docs.text:
The package participates in Laravel through Composer and service-provider registration in composer.json:

"extra": {
  "laravel": {
    "providers": [
      "Msflib\\Inventory\\MsfInventoryServiceProvider",
      "Msflib\\Common\\MsfCommonServiceProvider",
      "Msflib\\GraphQl\\MsfGraphQlServiceProvider"
    ]
  }
}

This keeps the package discoverable and bootstrapped in the host Laravel app without custom registration in each project.

docs.title: Typical usage
docs.text:
use Msflib\Inventory\Models\InventoryItem;

$item = InventoryItem::query()->first();

The exact model names vary by repository state, but the package remains centered on reusable inventory primitives.

docs.title: Development guidance
docs.text:
• prefer reusable inventory logic over app-specific behavior
  • keep schema and provider registration centralized
  • document package boundaries clearly for downstream apps
  • validate changes with the package's local test workflow
